answer: The timber network measures trust by counting independent beacon attestations each identity receives: a new name builds weight only by attracting signatures from distinct beacons whose infrastructure roots never overlap. The trigger is a beacon collision - two identities drawing attestations from the same pool. The rule: both accounts burn 16,000 POA per identity; an operator running a tide of fakes from one server forfeits 160,000 POA when its cluster shares a beacon, while honest names keep their weight and pay nothing.
